text:
caroline: Heads-up — high-priority customer ticket: their JSON consumer is failing intermittently. They say ~5% of responses are no longer valid JSON. Happens during peak traffic windows. attaching sample.

sam: Can you paste the raw response and the request id?

caroline: Request ID: rq_0a1b2c3d. Request body (simplified):```
POST /v1/generate
{"mode":"json","prompt":"return {\"items\": [ {\"id\": 1, \"value\": \"ok\"} ] }"}
```

caroline: Response body (customer sees parsing error):```
{"items":"{\"id\":1,\"value\":\"ok\"}","provenance":"fallback:quant-v2:trace=abc123"}
```

mike: Whoa — response has items as a string instead of an array. Looks like the fallback variant serialized the inner JSON as a string + added a provenance field. That will break strict parsers.

eng-bot: routing-log: rq_0a1b2c3d -> route: primary=model-stable-1, fallback=model-quant-v2, selected=fallback due to capacity_threshold.

sam: Is this specific to quantized variants? We had one bug where a wrapper was added to preserve debugging info.

caroline: Customer reproduced with a minimal curl and got the same. They included a snap of the split-second where latency spiked and route switched.

nia_support: Asking customer for the full raw HTTP response headers + whether they use streaming. Also requested SDK version.

sebastian: Quick triage: likely our fallback adds a provenance envelope when model returns text instead of structured tokens. We may be applying a shim that serializes the original payload into a string field to avoid losing data. That's acceptable for text mode but not for strict json mode.

sam: Repro notes: 1) set model=auto / enable_smart_routing=true 2) send json-mode request 3) induce load to trigger capacity fallbacks. Observed payloads contain either proper JSON or an enveloped string + provenance keys.

mike: Workaround for customer: pin model=model-stable-1 or set routing_preference=prefer_stable in the API call. Also validate after parsing and try to coerce string->json if you control client.

caroline: Customer can't pin (they rely on auto for cost). Would be good to either stop enveloping structured responses or expose an opt-out flag for adding provenance keys. They filed a support SLA escalation.

sebastian: Action items: 1) Eng-runtime: audit fallback code path that handles incompatible outputs and see why it wraps structured output into string. 2) Product: add a flag to suppress provenance injection for json-mode endpoints. 3) Support: provide mitigation steps to customer (pin variant or post-parse coercion) and collect more logs.

sam: Can eng-runtime dump the exact transform? If we changed formatting to avoid tokenization loss, we need to ensure we preserve structured contract for json-mode requests.

eng-bot: deploy-annotation: created incident ENG-7845 - "fallback wrapper breaks json-mode contract". Assigned to @sebastian. Priority P2 (customer SLA).

sebastian: I'll start a small repro harness and run with routing debug on. Caroline — can you ask the customer to try one more run with header `X-Redwood-Debug: routing=true` and paste the full body+headers? Also capture whether response was chunked.

caroline: On it. Sent instructions. I'll update thread when we get the debug output.

sam: FYI — if we need an emergency workaround we could stop smart routing for json-mode globally until fix is out, but that's drastic. Prefer a targeted config per-customer.

mike: Noted. I'll hold on making code changes until we have exact repro and logs.

caroline: Customer uploaded debug log. Key excerpt:```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
X-Request-Id: rq_0a1b2c3d

{"items":"{\"id\":1,\"value\":\"ok\"}","_rdw_prov":"fallback:model-quant-v2;reason=latency_shed"}
```

sebastian: Looks reproducible. I can reproduce locally by forcing route to quant-v2. Root cause: when model returns text that we detect as JSON-like we attempted to preserve the "raw_text" by embedding it, but we failed to coerce when the original returned JSON object tokens. We'll push a patch to keep structured objects as actual JSON when request mode==json.

sam: ETA on patch?

sebastian: I'll aim for a hotfix branch today, deploy to canary within 4 hours. If successful, we can roll to-prod and coordinate with support to lift the mitigation.

caroline: Thanks — I'll relay to customer and keep SLA updated. :+1:

nia_support: Adding note to ticket: advise client to implement defensive parse that attempts json decode on string fields named "items" if tolerable.

caroline: Closing loop once patch is live.
